title: Your logbook is only honest if your reps are.
hook: Your logbook is only honest if your reps are.
caption:
Your logbook is only honest if your reps are.

Adding five pounds does not automatically mean you progressed.

If you shortened the range, changed your setup, rushed the eccentric or used significantly more momentum, you didn’t improve the same movement. You created a different version that allowed you to move more weight.

That distinction matters because the logbook is supposed to help us make decisions.

If the standard stays consistent, I can see whether strength is improving, whether the rep target needs to change and whether the exercise is still productive.

title: YOUR SQUAT TECHNIQUE MATTERS 🏋️‍♀️
hook: YOUR SQUAT TECHNIQUE MATTERS 🏋️‍♀️
caption:
YOUR SQUAT TECHNIQUE MATTERS 🏋️‍♀️

Before adding more weight, make sure you’ve mastered the fundamentals.

Here are 5 common squat mistakes to watch for:

1️⃣ Knees collapsing inward without control.
2️⃣ Heels lifting off the ground.
3️⃣ Losing control of your spinal position.
4️⃣ Cutting your range of motion unnecessarily.
5️⃣ Rushing through every repetition.

✅ Keep your feet stable.
✅ Move through a comfortable, controlled range.
✅ Brace your core and maintain balance.
✅ Increase weight gradually as your technique improves.

Remember: Good training isn’t about lifting the heaviest weight.

title: Changing exercises can feel like progress - but novelty is not the same as muscle growth.
hook: Changing exercises can feel like progress - but novelty is not the same as muscle growth.
caption:
Changing exercises can feel like progress - but novelty is not the same as muscle growth.

An exercise needs time to become stable, repeatable and measurable.

If you constantly replace movements, improvements may simply come from learning the new exercise. Meanwhile, you never collect enough consistent data to determine whether you are actually progressing.

Before replacing an exercise, ask:

- Can I effectively load the intended muscle? 
- Can I repeat the same setup and execution? 
- Are my reps, load or control improving? 
- Does the exercise feel comfortable for my joints?

title: Most of your sets never reach the muscle fibers that grow the most. I’m Luca, and I explain training by the mechanism.
hook: Most of your sets never reach the muscle fibers that grow the most. I’m Luca, and I explain training by the mechanism.
caption:
Most of your sets never reach the muscle fibers that grow the most. I’m Luca, and I explain training by the mechanism.

Most people stop a set when it starts to burn, rest a minute and go again. Set after set, month after month, and the muscle barely changes.

But your body has a fixed order for which fibers it uses, and most sets end right before the best ones join.

About 2.5 hours of training a week built my physique.

I go by the mechanism: every working set to real failure, a lot of protein, and only the extras that are actually worth it.
